summary: An excerpt from a novel (labeled 'Book 3 — part 39') in which the narrator, Ms. James, meets Alex Goddard, a charismatic man who runs a place offering infertility treatment and adoption services. She describes his appearance, including a statue of Shiva, and recalls Aldous Huxley's view of men who control others with their minds. Goddard is casual but guarded, discourages publicity, and deflects her question about the adoption service to someone else.
one_line: Ms. James meets the charismatic Alex Goddard at his facility, probing its adoption service while he deflects publicity questions.
key_facts: The narrator is addressed as Ms. James and is a writer whose work Alex Goddard admires.
Alex Goddard says he is a great admirer of Ms. James's work and wanted to provide her orientation personally.
The narrator recalls a statue of Shiva whose lower left hand points down at a foot planted on a small dwarf representing the human ego.
The narrator attributes to Aldous Huxley the observation that a man who controls others with his mind needs intelligence, a will of iron, and uncompromising self-confidence.
Huxley's controlling man is described as having a slightly remote manner, a glittering eye, and a voice like a Pied Piper's.
The narrator senses a false note in Goddard, who seems to be being a little too casual.
Goddard says the place does not encourage publicity.
Goddard says he welcomes visitors who have come because of infertility, as Ramala said the narrator mentioned in her call.
Goddard earlier made a phone call trying to intimidate Paula Marks.
The narrator says she is interested in neither a film nor infertility treatment and is hoping to learn about the adoption service.
The narrator is considering someday making a documentary about this place.
Goddard's eyes shift to somewhere lost in the ozone when asked about the adoption service.
Goddard says the adoption service is not something he handles personally.
The narrator mentions Carly and Paula as people connected to Goddard's work, described as miracle-worker treatment.
